purpose: Measure whether FactCollector can reuse exact engine method resolution without rebuilding a receiver MRO for every inferred call while retaining bounded transient memory.

change.exact_callee_return: After ordinary MRO and visibility resolution selects a ResolvedMethodCallee, return inference reads only that callee's exact declaration ranges instead of resolving its owner as a new receiver.
change.query_cache: One revision-bound AnalysisQueryCache per source collection memoizes resolved private, public, and protected callees and invalidates on engine identity or semantic-revision change.
change.admission_bound: At most 64 resolved-callee query entries are retained per source collection. Additional unique lookups compute normally without entering the cache.
change.semantic_boundary: The cache contains query results only. File facts still enter through ordinary per-file replacement, and local same-pass return facts retain priority over engine-owned facts.

correctness.semantic_replacement_invalidation_regres: all cache families replaced on engine revision change

rejected_variants.name: unbounded callee plus callee-return caches
rejected_variants.decision: Rejected. Active semantic completion improved, but median peak RSS exceeded the explicit 10% ceiling.

rejected_variants.name: 256-entry callee plus callee-return caches
rejected_variants.decision: Rejected. A count bound did not make the duplicated callee-return catalog fit the memory ceiling.

rejected_variants.name: 128-entry resolved-callee-only cache
rejected_variants.decision: Rejected. Removing the duplicate return cache nearly met the ceiling, but median RSS remained 3.38 MB above it.

decision: Accepted at the 64-entry bound. Exact navigation, persistent-product provenance, cache invalidation, and the full local library gate remain correct. Active-project semantic completion improved 4.285% and dependency navigation improved 2.644%, while terminal wall remained effectively flat and median RSS stayed 18.1 MB below the predeclared 10% ceiling. This does not close the 15-second exhaustive-workspace or five-second active semantic targets.
